children: The Maldives has fully settled the $150 million Treasury Bill (T-bill) facility subscribed by State Bank of India, repaying the final $50 million tranche on September 17,  but India has borne nearly $45 million in interest payments on the facility over the past five years, the MEA has said.

“India and Maldives have a longstanding development partnership….It may also be noted that while the principal amount of the T-bills was paid by the Government of Maldives, the interest payment of all the $150 million T-Bills over the past five years, was borne by the Government of India. The total amount paid by India in interest settlement was close to $45 million,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in response to a question at a media briefing on Friday.
These bills were subscribed by SBI since 2019 and were extended six times, each for a year, till now.

India has also extended a ₹3,000 crore  currency swap facility to the Maldives to support the Maldivian financial system, Jaiswal noted. “In addition, Government of India has also subscribed to $350 million worth of T-Bonds which are valid till 2029 and 2030,” he added.

The Maldivian government has credited the repayment to disciplined debt management. In a post on X on Thursday, Maldives’ Foreign Minister Hassan Zareer said the country had completed repayment of the $150 million borrowed through SBI in 2019, settling the final $50 million instalment. He added that under President Mohamed Muizzu’s leadership, the government continued to manage debt responsibly through advance planning and regular contributions to the Sovereign Development Fund, and that arrangements for uninterrupted imports of fuel, staple foods and medicines remained fully secured.

“Under the leadership of President (Mohamed Muizzu) our government continues to manage debt responsibly through advance planning and regular contributions to the Sovereign Development Fund. Arrangements for uninterrupted imports of fuel, staple foods and medicines remain fully secured,” he posted.

title: India has borne nearly $45 million in interest payments on Maldive’s T-bill facility: MEA
